description: Open-source marketing automation for a 5-100 person team: segments, campaigns, landing pages, lead scoring and e-mail journeys sent through the operator's own mail infrastructure.
authMethod: Proxy gate only - Mautic keeps its own login (no OIDC/SAML in the free core)

notes: Campaign and segment mail is sent from a second container running the cron role; a web container alone renders the product but sends nothing. Deliverability (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) is an operator responsibility, not a platform one. `imageRef` is the tag the definition runs — the vendored wrapper `seamnex/mautic:7.2.2`, which the service declares as its own `build:` so the platform produces it in the build stage from platform/upstream/D02-01 rather than pulling it (ADR-BE-40); the pinned `mautic/mautic:7.2.2-apache` image is the base it wraps. Because the artefact is local, `imageDigest` is reference data: the enforced pin is the image id the host built, recorded per instance on the first deployment.
deviation: Upstream `mautic/mautic` ships neither a Compose file nor a Dockerfile, and its Docker distribution starts Apache with the product *uninstalled*. Four deliberate changes, recorded row by row in platform/upstream/D02-01/README.md: (1) the application is a thin layer over the pinned upstream image, declared as the service's own `build:` with `pull_policy: never`, so the executor builds `seamnex/mautic:7.2.2` in the build stage and the tag can never resolve to a registry's idea of it; (2) a MariaDB service is added, because the catalog has always declared `database` as a dependency and without it the product reached its own error page; (3) the cron container is kept, because campaigns and segments are sent by scheduled commands, so a web container alone renders a product that never sends a mail; (4) `ports:` is written as `expose:` — the platform publishes no host port and the edge reaches the container on the instance network. The first-boot install runs in `seamnex-bootstrap.sh` (`bin/console mautic:install`) before the image's own entrypoint, because only a CLI install makes a deployment usable without a browser, and `config/local.php` is the marker that keeps a restart from reinstalling.
